''rioavefc.pt''. | owner = [[Evangelos Marinakis]] | chrtitle = President | manager = [[Vasco Seabra]] | mgrtitle = Head coach | league = [[Primeira Liga]] | season = [[2025–26 Primeira Liga|2025–26]] | position = Primeira Liga, 12th of 18 | current = 2026–27 Rio Ave F.C. season | website = {{URL|rioavefc.pt}} | pattern_la1 = _rioave2627h | pattern_b1 = _rioave2627h | pattern_ra1 = _rioave2627h | pattern_sh1 = _rioave2627h | pattern_so1 = _rioave2627hl | leftarm1 = FFFFFF | body1 = FFFFFF | rightarm1 = FFFFFF | shorts1 = 007711 | socks1 = 007711 | pattern_la2 = _rioave2627a | pattern_b2 = _rioave2627a | pattern_ra2 = _rioave2627a | pattern_sh2 = _rioave2627a | pattern_so2 = _rioave2627al | leftarm2 = 87ceeb | body2 = 000055 | rightarm2 = 87ceeb | shorts2 = 000055 | socks2 = 000055 | pattern_la3 = | pattern_b3 = | pattern_ra3 = | pattern_sh3 = | pattern_so3 = | leftarm3 = | body3 = | rightarm3 = | shorts3 = | socks3 = }} '''Rio Ave Futebol Clube''', commonly known as '''Rio Ave''' ({{IPA|pt|ˈʁi.u ˈavɨ|}}), is a [[Football in Portugal|Portuguese]] professional [[Association football|football]] club based in [[Vila do Conde]], that competes in the [[Primeira Liga]]. The club is named after the [[Ave River]], which flows through the town and into the [[Atlantic Ocean]]. Founded in 1939, they play their home matches at [[Estádio do Rio Ave FC]], also known as the Estádio dos Arcos. Built in 1985, the current stadium seats approximately 5,300 people. The club's home colours are green and white striped shirts. Meanwhile, the shorts and socks have historically alternated between green or white.{{cite web|url=https://www.colours-of-football.com/colours03/por/rioave/rioave_1.html|title=Colours of Football - Rio Ave FC|publisher=Colours of Football|accessdate=8 April 2023}} [[Portugal national football team|Portuguese internationals]] [[Alfredo Castro (footballer)|Alfredo]], [[Paulinho Santos]], [[Quim (footballer, born 1959)|Quim]], [[Rui Jorge]] and [[Fábio Coentrão]] started their careers at the club. Goalkeepers [[Jan Oblak]] and [[Ederson (footballer, born 1993)|Ederson]] are some famous talents that were part of this side. The ''Vilacondenses''' best top-tier league finish was fifth in the [[1981–82 Primeira Divisão|1981–82]], [[2017–18 Primeira Liga|2017–18]] and [[2019–20 Primeira Liga|2019–20]] seasons.{{Cite web|date=19 July 2020|title=Rio Ave bate recorde de pontos na liga, Vitória já não chegará à Europa|trans-title=Rio Ave sets record for league points, Vitória will no longer reach Europe|url=https://tribunaexpresso.pt/futebol-nacional/2020-07-19-Rio-Ave-bate-recorde-de-pontos-na-liga-Vitoria-ja-nao-chegara-a-Europa|access-date=2021-12-11|website=Tribuna Expresso|language=pt}} They reached the [[1984 Taça de Portugal Final]], where they lost to [[FC Porto|Porto]] 4–1, and the [[2014 Taça de Portugal Final]], where they lost to [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] 1–0.{{cite news|title=Rio Ave beat Braga to reach final|url=http://www.kingfut.com/2014/04/17/kokas-rio-ave-qualifies-portuguese-cup-final/}} With this result, Rio Ave qualified for the [[2014–15 UEFA Europa League]], their first participation in a major [[UEFA competitions|European competition]]."}}
